questions.q: Which iconic building by the Pasig River is considered Juan Arellano's neoclassical masterpiece, featuring 14 massive Ionic columns?
o: The National Museum of Fine Arts
questions.n: Completed in 1926, this building is a textbook example of Neoclassicism and is one of Arellano's most famous works.

questions.q: The Metropolitan Theater (The Met) is Juan Arellano's most famous foray into which architectural style, often called 'The Grand Old Dame of Manila'?
questions.n: The Met is a world-class example of Art Deco, featuring localized Filipino motifs like mangoes and bananas in its carvings.

questions.q: Juan Arellano designed several provincial capitols. Which of these is noted for its 'U-shaped' plan and grand neoclassical facade in the Visayas?
questions.n: This is one of Arellano's most famous provincial works, serving as a landmark of American-era civic pride in Cebu.

questions.q: Before becoming an architect, Juan Arellano was actually trained as a:
questions.n: His training as a painter heavily influenced the highly decorative and aesthetic quality of his architectural works.

questions.q: True or False: Juan Arellano's design for the Metropolitan Theater included sculptures by Francesco Riccardo Monti.
questions.n: Arellano frequently collaborated with Monti to integrate world-class sculpture into his architectural designs.

questions.q: Juan Arellano's Metropolitan Theater is famous for 'Sari-Sari' Art Deco. Which of the following is a specific example of the localized motifs found in its ornamentation?
o: Abstract symbols from the Industrial Revolution
Native Philippine flora such as bananas and mangoes
questions.n: Arellano integrated local natural elements into the geometric patterns of Art Deco to create a distinctly Filipino aesthetic.

questions.q: The Manila Central Post Office features a 'crepidoma.' What is the purpose of this architectural element in Arellano's design?
o: It serves as the hidden basement for mail sorting
It is the stepped base that elevates the building and its columns
It is the decorative crown at the top of the columns
It is a decorative frieze depicting the history of mail
questions.n: In classical architecture, the crepidoma provides a grand, elevated foundation that signifies the building's importance.

questions.q: Which major urban planning role did Juan Arellano play during his tenure at the Bureau of Public Works?
o: He planned the relocation of the capital to Quezon City
He supervised the implementation of the Burnham Plan for Manila
He drafted the master plan for the city of Baguio
He designed the first subway system in Asia
questions.n: As a lead architect in the BPW, he was responsible for designing the buildings that fulfilled Burnham's vision for a grand civic center.

questions.q: The 'Legislative Building' (now the National Museum of Fine Arts) was originally intended for a different purpose. What was it?
questions.n: The building was initially designed as a library before it was modified to accommodate the Philippine Legislature.

questions.q: Juan Arellano was known for his 'Beaux-Arts' influence. What is a key characteristic of this architectural education style?
o: Organic shapes inspired by the forest
Symmetry, formal design, and abundant classical ornamentation
The use of lightweight, impermanent materials
questions.n: Beaux-Arts training emphasized rigorous academic classical forms combined with elaborate decorative details.

questions.q: The Cebu Provincial Capitol features a famous quote inscribed on its facade. What does this indicate about Arellano's approach to civic architecture?
o: He was forced to use text because he ran out of stone carvings
He believed buildings should remain silent and mysterious
He viewed architecture as a tool for public communication and civic identity
He was trying to hide flaws in the concrete with text
questions.n: Inscriptions and monuments were used to inspire pride and reinforce the purpose of the government structure.

questions.q: True or False: After World War II, Juan Arellano retired and refused to work on any reconstruction projects in Manila.
questions.n: He was actually deeply saddened by the destruction of his works and shifted his focus back to painting in his later years.

questions.q: In the Metropolitan Theater, the 'stained glass' facade is actually made of what material that allowed for its vibrant colors?
questions.n: The combination of colored glass and stylized ironwork allowed Arellano to create the theater's glowing 'jewel box' effect.

questions.q: Juan Arellano's design for the 'Villamor Hall' (now the UP Manila College of Music) is characterized by which of the following?
o: Elegant neoclassical proportions and a grand portico
A futuristic design with no visible support
A design that mimicked a ship
questions.n: This building reflects the academic dignity of the University of the Philippines during the American colonial period.

questions.q: Juan Arellano was a key architect in the design of the 'Commonwealth Triumphal Arch.' What was the fate of this project?
o: It was completed but later demolished by the Americans
It stands today in the center of Rizal Park
It was never constructed due to the outbreak of World War II
It was turned into a housing project for veterans
questions.n: The war interrupted the ambitious architectural plans of the Commonwealth government, including this grand monument.
